newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian police investigate military sex charges.
newsitem.headline: Australian police investigate military sex charges.

text.p: Australian Federal Police are investigating three charges of serious sexual assault involving Australian Defence Force Academy male cadets against their female colleagues, a military spokesman said on Monday.
The three female cadets claim they were assaulted at the officer training academy in Canberra earlier this year, defence force spokesman Brigadier Adrian D'Hage told Reuters.
A total of five charges of sexual assault by male military cadets at the 1,000-strong academy have been received by the academy command in 1995-96, D'Hage said.
Only three cases were referred to police.

"At a certain level we say there is a case to answer and we refer it to the Australian Federal Police or state police," said D'Hage. "We have the ability to investigate internally, but we prefer not to do so.
"When we call in the Australian Federal Police that sends a very powerful message to those people doing the wrong thing."
D'Hage said the incidence of sexual assault in the Australian military had fallen by about 25 percent in the past two years as a result of educational programmes.
In 1994-95 the Australian military received a total of 110 sexual harassment allegations, compared with 84 in 1995-96.
In 1993, a naval board of inquiry found that five female sailors were regularly sexually harassed during war exercises.

The U.S. Army is being rocked by a sex scandal which has seen 10 drill instructors and other trainers charged with violations ranging from rape to "fraternising" with female recruits at the U.S. Army's Aberdeen Proving Ground in Maryland and at Fort Leonard Wood in Missouri.
In 1991 the U.S. Navy was embroiled in scandal when male Navy and Marine pilots abused females at a Las Vegas hotel.
